svg.title: StillWedge GPU: a linear execution walkthrough
svg.desc: Twenty-four numbered stages, read top to bottom: CPU geometry and particle setup, upload, GPU cell-list construction, adaptive time step, two symplectic neighbor passes, integration, batched state readback, asynchronous CPU output and finalization. Blue denotes CPU work, green GPU work, amber output work. Repetition is indicated by stage numbers rather than crossing arrows. This is a source-based flow diagram, not a measured timeline or simulation result.
svg.text: StillWedge: what the GPU actually does
Read straight down. Numbers match the detailed, source-linked walkthrough.
Exact script, not the filename: NoMDBC + symplectic + radial interactions.
Direct execution currently calls the solver twice. This diagram follows ONE invocation.
No ghost-node correction, shifting, floating-body physics or kernel-sum output is active.
The physical case (schematic, not simulation output)
Plus a small device-control readback per batch
STARTUP: build the inputs once, then hand the evolving state to the GPU.

g.text: Enter the example
Load the GPU package; include polygon helper definitions; enter one run.
run_still_wedge(); using SPHExampleGPU; include(...)
The included generator does not export CSVs or run its own main block.
Construct the physical constants
Reference density, spacing, sound speed, gravity, viscosity, diffusion and CFL.
SimulationConstants{Float32}(...)
CFL = 0.5; c0 approximately 42.48576 m/s; density-diffusion coefficient = 0.1.
Describe tank and water as polygons
Fixed floor, side walls and hollow wedge shell; water occupies the region around it.
still_wedge_2d_polygons() -> tank, water
Meshes.jl PolyArea geometry; no GPU computation yet.
Sample a common particle lattice
Boundaries claim shared surfaces first; fluid points are strictly inside their polygon.
ParticleRegion -> sample_particles -> particle_lattice / owns
Result: 580 fixed and 2,447 fluid positions with no overlap.
Initialize hydrostatic density and particle groups
Walls start at reference density; deeper fluid starts slightly denser.
hydrostatic_density(...) -> SPHGeometry{2,Float32}(...)
Hydrostatic level is the highest fluid center, y = 0.48 m, not the 0.5 m outline.
Configure metadata, host arrays and logging
Create structure-of-arrays state, one-based IDs, zero velocity and acceleration.
SimulationMetaData -> SimulationLogger -> AllocateDataStructures
CleanUpSimulationFolder removes stale VTKHDF output in the selected save directory.
Choose the kernel, models and time integrator
Wendland C2, artificial viscosity, linear density diffusion, symplectic stepping.
SPHKernelInstance(...) -> RunSimulation(...)
The default integrator requires two neighbor evaluations per accepted step.
Validate CUDA and resolve output fields
Select radial arithmetic; map requested pressure output to a density download.
start_runtime!; radial_interactions_supported; resolve_output_variables!
NoMDBC skips the normals-file load and every ghost-node boundary correction.
Upload once and allocate GPU workspaces
Particles, sort scratch, density derivatives, predictor density, caches and control state.
upload_particles; ReductionWorkspace; CellListWorkspace; GPUSupportArrays
MotionArrays and FloatingArrays are inactive; StepState starts with a forced rebuild.
Prepare output and save the initial particle frame
Create particle/grid files, two pinned staging buffers and collector/writer tasks.
SetupVTKOutput; OutputDownload; InitializeLogger; save_particle_data
Particle frame at t = 0; the empty initial grid call does not write a grid frame.
Start an output interval
Set the next physical-time deadline; choose cooperative lanes for each particle.
SimulationLoop -> choose_lanes; next_output_time; set_output_time!
Checked GPU: 4 lanes/particle; 95 blocks of 128 threads per neighbor pass.
Prime the reduction; request the first cell-list build
Initial reduction supplies dt limits; the oversized displacement bound stops integration.
launch_step_reduction! -> reduce_kernel!; finish_kernel! -> STOP_REBUILD
Startup only: the first attempt builds infrastructure, not a physical time step.
Bin, prefix-scan, sort and reorder particles
Build candidate cell ranges; initialize fixed predictors and cell-relative positions.
prepare_cell_grid! -> rebuild_cell_list! -> update_cell_list!
Histogram/scatter use atomics. This stage repeats only when a rebuild is requested.
Enqueue a batch, usually by CUDA-graph replay
Estimate up to 32 attempts; reuse captured launch sequences with stable device inputs.
batch_size -> launch_step_graph! -> enqueue_step!
Each accepted step is stages 15-19. Attempts after a device stop are no-ops.
Choose dt and check whether the attempt may run
Combine previous reductions; check deadline and accumulated displacement.
launch_finish! -> finish_kernel! -> step_reduce / block_reduce
May set STOP_REBUILD or STOP_OUTPUT. Otherwise the following kernels are active.
FIRST neighbor pass: accepted full state
Cache pressure/inverse density; gather continuity, diffusion and acceleration.
enqueue_state_derivative! -> launch_prepare_interactions! / launch_interactions!
3 rows x 3 cells; circular support test; lane-local sums; warp shuffle; lane zero writes.
Predict the HALF state
Add gravity; predict positions, velocities and densities over dt/2.
launch_half_step! -> half_step_kernel!
Refresh half-state pressure/inverse density and local positions. Fixed walls do not move.
SECOND neighbor pass: predicted half state
Repeat the same pair physics using half positions, velocities, densities and caches.
launch_interactions! -> interaction_kernel!
Overwrite the derivatives with midpoint values; reuse the candidate cell ranges.
Accept the full step and commit time
Update density/velocity; move x by v_half*dt; reduce next-step limits and displacement.
launch_final_step! -> final_step_kernel!; launch_commit! -> commit_kernel!
The 12-block reduction is fused into integration. Another queued attempt returns to 15.
Read the small batch state and respond
Transfer time, dt, flags and conditional grid header, not the full particle arrays.
prepare_cell_grid! -> readback! -> sync_meta_data!
Rebuild? Do 13. More work? Do 14. Output deadline crossed? Continue to 21.
Enqueue an output snapshot
Download positions, selected particle fields and cell IDs into a pinned staging frame.
LogStep; enqueue_download! -> copy_async!; OutputFrameJob
Completion event protects the snapshot. Same-stream copies precede later GPU writes.
Collect, stage and write particles plus occupied cells
CPU tasks reconstruct pressure and buffer HDF5 writes while the GPU can continue.
collect_download! -> stage_particle_slot -> write_frame -> flush_frames!
Grid export bins current snapshot positions. Backpressure waits; frames are not dropped.
Repeat intervals until accepted time is greater than 4.00 s
If not finished, return to 11. Reuse GPU arrays, graphs and output buffers.
RunSimulation loop: TotalTime > SimulationTime ? finish : next interval
Output deadlines are crossed; adaptive dt is not clipped to hit them exactly.
Drain output, download the final state and finalize
Wait for workers; flush/close files; update full host state; write visualization state.
close_output_streams!; download_particles!; finalize_output!
AutoOpenParaview, LogFinal and AutoOpenLogFile finish one invocation.

svg.text: CPU organizes and saves. GPU gathers nearby-particle contributions twice per step, then integrates.
All active project functions and small helpers are listed in StillWedgeGPUWalkthrough.md at the matching stage.
Source-based flow, not a performance timeline. Lane count is hardware-dependent. Full details and exclusions: companion guide.
